42f0629777: Microsoft is testing a new shader compiler for Xbox Series X and Series S that could improve game performance without hardware changes. The experimental compiler is based on ACO, an open-source project from Mesa. Microsoft reports improvements ranging from 2% to 16% compared with its existing Xbox shader compiler.

The feature is included in the October 2026 Microsoft Game Development Kit (GDK). According to Microsoft, developers can use ACO as an alternative optimization tool for shader compilation and runtime performance. The results depend on the game engine, content and existing shader bottlenecks.

ACO, short for AMD Compiler, is already used by Mesa’s RADV Vulkan driver for AMD GPUs on Linux. The compiler converts shader instructions into machine code optimized for AMD graphics architectures. It is also used on systems such as Valve’s Steam Deck, which runs games using the RADV driver.

The Xbox Series X and Series S both use AMD RDNA 2 graphics hardware. Microsoft is now evaluating whether the same compiler technology can improve performance on its consoles. b1a0bcfa14: ASUS has detailed a new DDR5 memory-training behavior introduced with AMD AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A. Selected ASUS AM5 motherboards now have beta BIOS releases that include the change. Boards equipped with a Q-Code display show a counting sequence during memory training.

853f8baa73: Apple’s new MacBook Pro with a tandem OLED display is receiving complaints from users reporting headaches, dizziness and eye discomfort. The issue may be related to pulse-width modulation (PWM), which controls display brightness by rapidly changing light output. Independent testing has measured a relatively low flickering frequency of 240 Hz on the new 14-inch model.

According to Notebookcheck’s review of the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the PROLED XDR display, flickering occurs at brightness settings of 99% or lower. The publication measured a frequency of 240 Hz with a 56% modulation amplitude. This behavior persists despite the display also using DC dimming across its brightness range.

PWM flickering is common on OLED displays and is not necessarily visible to users. However, some people are sensitive to these brightness fluctuations, which may cause headaches or eye strain during extended use. The 240 Hz PWM frequency is separate from the MacBook Pro’s 120 Hz display refresh rate.

For comparison, Notebookcheck previously measured PWM at 14,880 Hz on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M4 Pro processor and Mini-LED display. This is 62 times higher than the frequency recorded on the new OLED model. Higher PWM frequencies are generally less likely to cause discomfort for sensitive users, although the frequency alone does not determine how a display affects an individual.

22688e79a9: As governments scramble to make AI safer, who gets to write the rules could be just as important as what they say.

But just because it was better behaved on the surface didn’t mean it was entirely safe. OpenAI said Astra’s written reasoning was harder to monitor than its predecessor’s when they were testing its ability to evade oversight. The model began to recognize when it was being watched and altered its explanations to suit the study, making it harder to tell when it was actually doing something they didn’t want.
It’s a classic problem for AI alignment experts to try and resolve.

For years, developers have relied on monitoring an AI model's chain of thought — its written working — to understand what it is doing. But if increasingly powerful AI models become better at hiding their reasoning processes, that oversight becomes harder to do.

0624b47944: AMD says Ozaki FP64 emulation is no replacement for the real thing when it's needed.

Over the past few years, Nvidia has reallocated die area on its data center GPUs to favor the lower-precision matrix math that boosts the operations needed for much of modern AI inference. That reallocation only makes business sense, as the total addressable market for AI compute has exploded while the demand for double-precision math in large supercomputing installations has remained flat by comparison.

To make up for the lack of native FP64 support, Nvidia has turned to techniques that allow it to emulate FP64 operations using methods like the Ozaki schemes. But AMD claims this kind of emulation is nowhere close to a replacement for native double-precision processing for a few reasons—hence continued development of specialized products like the MI430X.

For one, AMD notes that Ozaki emulation assumes that the workload in question resembles a dense general matrix multiply (GEMM). In its own application profiling, the company says "less than 10%" of HPC workloads perform dense GEMM operations, so this emulation is a good replacement for native compute. Dense linear algebra is the one common workload for which AMD says Ozaki emulation is a natural fit.

e0126d7463: Semiconductor manufacturers are increasing automation to boost the productivity of existing fabs

According to a report by Seoul Economic Daily, the initiative aims to establish common technical specifications that would allow robots from different manufacturers to share charging equipment, reducing the cost and complexity of deploying large robotic fleets across semiconductor manufacturing facilities. The broader goal is to accelerate factory automation, particularly in older fabs, while laying the groundwork for fully autonomous semiconductor manufacturing.

So why are three of the world's biggest memory manufacturers, who are also competitors, coming together to establish standards for the robotics industry? What exactly does the collaboration involve? And what are the implications of something as seemingly minor as robot charging for the broader semiconductor and robotics industries?

Soaring demand for semiconductor memory chips used in AI infrastructure has driven manufacturers to automate as many production processes as possible to optimize manufacturing speed and capacity in existing facilities to increase output, while they build additional fabs. Modern semiconductor fabs already have extensive automation systems. However, even these facilities still require human workers for certain operations, such as moving materials between floors and unpacking products, that existing automation systems cannot perform. The issue is even more pronounced in older fabs, which generally have fewer automated material-handling systems and still rely on workers to move wafer containers using manual carts.

The patch only adds processor family and model identifiers to the Linux kernel. These definitions allow future updates to recognize the processors and apply hardware-specific support. Intel has also submitted separate GCC compiler patches for Razor Lake and Coral Rapids.
c8aa09ae03: Powering them put out an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of CO2, 2–3x a 2018 estimate.

Hyperscale data centers, in this case, refer to sites run by a hyperscale cloud or content provider, or a colocation operator who serves one, with a capacity in the tens of megawatts. The 675 candidate sites came from data vendor Baxtel, with 403 confirmed with satellite imagery and building-footprint maps, at an average capacity of 39.9 MW and a median of 36 MW.

Nobody officially counts what the data centers actually draw from the grid. Instead, the electricity is estimated by multiplying each site’s maximum capacity by the hours in a year and an estimate of how hard the data centers run. For CO2 and the source mix, each site is placed in its grid region, of 23 total in the study, with a regional average mix from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). These are then multiplied and added up for the total number. Such estimation methods may reduce the strength of arguments against data center buildouts.
The power is also not evenly laid out, with 142 of the sites located in Virginia alone, taking 21.4 TWh, or about a quarter.
51794529c6: Samsung, SK hynix and Micron have failed to dismiss a class-action lawsuit accusing the three memory manufacturers of coordinating DRAM production cuts and restricting supply to increase prices. US District Judge Noël Wise rejected their joint motion on November 14, allowing the case to proceed in the Northern District of California.

The lawsuit was filed on June 25, 2026, by 17 consumers and small businesses from five US states. The plaintiffs allege that the companies coordinated production reductions beginning in late 2022, shifted manufacturing capacity toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and reduced conventional DRAM availability. According to the complaint, the three manufacturers controlled more than 91% of global DRAM revenue in the third quarter of 2025.

The complaint specifically points to the companies’ decisions to reduce DDR4 production between April and June 2025. It also questions why none of the three manufacturers meaningfully expanded conventional DRAM capacity despite rising prices. The plaintiffs allege that conventional DRAM prices increased by nearly 700% over an 18-month period.

Micron’s decision to discontinue its Crucial consumer business in December 2025 is also cited. The court considered this closure alongside long-term HBM supply commitments and restrictions affecting conventional DRAM customers. Judge Wise found that the combined allegations provided sufficient grounds to continue the case, rather than dismiss it as ordinary competition between a small number of manufacturers.
e2cf4dd7fc: China has been at this for over two decades, and they're not slowing down.

Shenyang Aircraft Design and Research Institute, a research organization under the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), has been working on 3D-printed aircraft components since 2003. The impressively large 3D-printed components are the culmination of decades of research and development of various metal additive manufacturing techniques.

The engineers are no strangers to large 3D-printed components: in 2005, they achieved secondary load-bearing structures; then, in 2012, large primary load-bearing titanium alloy structures, earning additive manufacturing expert Wang Huaming and his team China’s National Technological Invention Award.

Recently, however, the team created a primary load-bearing structure even larger, at over 16.4 feet. The massive component is not printed in one piece, as printing such a large structure faces warping and cracking issues, as stated in Progress and Challenges of Laser Direct Manufacturing of Large Titanium Structural Components, published in the Chinese Journal of Lasers. To avoid these problems, two techniques were employed: Segmented Additive Manufacturing (SAM) and additive fusion joining. It sounds like fancy words to say it was printed separately and welded, and it technically wouldn’t be wrong — but the key distinction is that it is part of the whole workflow; basically, metal 3D printing into the intentionally designed gaps between the components and creating one whole printed piece.
c0795014b9: A GeForce RTX 5090 owner who previously reported a melted power connector has shared another update. This time, the problem concerns the repair itself. According to Redditor m0hm1, Overclockers UK returned the Palit RTX 5090 GameRock OC with a poorly soldered power connector, which subsequently detached from the PCB. The retailer has reportedly refused another warranty claim.

The original incident dates back to April 2026, when the owner discovered that the 16-pin power connector had melted while using NVIDIA’s supplied adapter. Overclockers UK initially rejected the warranty request, citing physical damage. However, after the case received attention on Reddit, the retailer’s management agreed to handle the RMA and arrange collection of the graphics card.

According to the latest update, the graphics card was returned with a replacement 12VHPWR connector that was visibly loose. The owner decided to test it using a new Thermal Grizzly WireView Pro 2, a monitoring device capable of measuring current distribution across individual power pins. On the first boot, the device immediately reported a current imbalance before the power reading dropped to 0W.

The owner claims the repair center failed to secure the connector properly, leaving weak solder joints and an improperly attached retention tab. Photos shared on Reddit show the connector detached from the PCB. The owner argues that the absence of visibly damaged copper pads or torn traces supports the theory of a failed soldering repair, although the exact cause has not been independently verified.
94ed499e51: AMD has released version 4.1.2 of its FidelityFX Super Resolution plugin for Unreal Engine 5. The update brings machine learning-based upscaling to Radeon RX 6000 graphics cards and select Ryzen processors with integrated Radeon graphics. It supports Unreal Engine versions 5.3 through 5.8.

The plugin is based on the FSR Redstone SDK 2.4, which we covered in October. AMD also updated the Unreal Engine plugin in August, adding support for Radeon RX 7000 GPUs. The latest release extends machine learning upscaling to RDNA 2 graphics cards and supported Ryzen-powered laptops, mini-PCs and gaming handhelds.

AMD uses two INT8 models for FSR Upscaling 4.1.2. Radeon RX 6000 GPUs and Ryzen AI Max processors use the full model, while other supported Ryzen processors use an optimized model that is less than half the size. AMD automatically selects the appropriate model based on the hardware. The plugin also includes FSR 3 as a fallback for unsupported GPUs.

The release includes FSR Frame Generation 4.0.2 and Frame Generation Swapchain 4.0.0. The latter enables Driver-Assisted Frame Pacing on Radeon RX 9000 GPUs. This feature delegates presentation timing to the AMD display driver to improve frame delivery and reduce CPU overhead. It requires Adrenalin Edition 26.10.1 or newer, while FSR Frame Generation 4.0.2 requires Windows 11.
022954f19c: China's LineShine, installed at the National Supercomputer Center in Shenzhen, offers sustained FP64 compute performance of 2.198 FP64 ExaFLOPS in the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark at 42.22 MW. The machine relies on the homegrown LingKun platform with 304-core Armx9-based LX2 processors clocked at 1.55 GHz (13,789,440 cores in total) and the proprietary LingQi interconnect. Unlike the other four exascale-class supercomputers, LineShine does not use any compute accelerators and exclusively relies on CPUs, which is largely why it only gains 3.6X performance when moving from FP64 to mixed-precision data, which is lower than systems that use low-precision accelerators.

America's most powerful El Capitan supercomputer at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory relies on AMD's Instinct MI300A accelerated processing units (APUs), and the HPE Cray EX255a platform delivers 1.809 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 29.69 MW, which makes it significantly more power-efficient than its rival from China. The Frontier supercomputer at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory, based on AMD's 3rd Generation EPYC processors and Instinct MI250X compute GPUs, achieves 1.353 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 24.61 MW. Meanwhile, Aurora at the Argonne National Laboratory, which uses Intel's Xeon CPU Max 9470 processors and Data Center GPU Max accelerators, offers 1.012 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 38.70 MW.
1750a0de16: The Bureau of Industry and Security has released an interim final rule to ensure physical restrictions cannot be bypassed by using cloud-based infrastructure.

Nvidia, for example, is only allowed to export its high-performance AI chips to companies that are on a whitelist. But amid ongoing claims of black market GPU sales and a recent crackdown on overseas AI GPU rentals from China, it has become clear that these restrictions perhaps aren't as robust as they were intended to be. Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs were even recently discovered in a data center used by China Telecom.

But while blocking the sale of physical goods is one thing, the cloud-based workaround is another entirely. Nvidia itself told data center operators earlier this month that they must limit remote access to their services — 51% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. But, again, it's unclear how effective that approach has been in ensuring access to powerful AI capabilities doesn't fall into the wrong hands, even if they're accessed remotely rather than in person.
The new BIS rule means that overseas data centers will be required to do more to limit access to their services where U.S-based technology is being used.
13226ef96b: A heterogeneous compute stack brings together quantum, HPC, and AI under one roof, a fleet that AMD is helping pilot at Oak Ridge National Laboratory alongside IBM. Tease is AMD’s corporate vice president of HPC and sovereign AI, who joined the company earlier this year after more than a decade at Lenovo (and, before that, another 13 years at IBM). We spoke with Tease ahead of SC26 to get a read on the state of HPC, how it intersects with AI, and what’s actually driving the research community in a time when computer chips are driving headlines about international espionage plots.

FP64 is important for HPC workloads because of its precision. FP64 is a hot-button issue, largely due to how Nvidia’s GPUs have progressed over the past two generations. Or rather, how they haven't progressed. Nvidia’s latest Rubin GPU has 33 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, which is lower than the four-year-old H100’s 34 TFLOPs of FP64. For context, AMD’s year-old Instinct MI355X peaks at 78.6 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, while its upcoming HPC-angled MI430X peaks at 288 TFLOPs.

Nvidia has leaned on emulation to drive FP64 performance higher, a tactic that AMD is now pushing back on, but regardless, it’s easy to see why the HPC world could feel left behind in this new AI era.
5e46de01b3: Lux is the first of two machines AMD is developing as part of a $1 billion deal with the DOE.

AMD’s representation in the top 10 is familiar. After debuting in June, China’s LineShine remains in the top slot. El Capitan, powered by AMD chips, is in the second slot, followed by Frontier in third, HPC7 in sixth, and HPC6 in eighth, the same as the most recent TOP500 list.

Lux was announced a little over a year ago in a $1 billion deal between the DOE and AMD to develop two supercomputers. This is the first of the two, and the first time it’s been on the TOP500. The system was built by HPE and developed by AMD and DOE as part of the U.S. government’s Genesis Mission. The machine is housed in Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF), alongside machines like Frontier.

Lux relies on over 4,000 Instinct MI355X GPUs separated into over 500 nodes. For HPC workloads using FP64, the machine is capable of 317 PetaFLOPS. For AI training, the machine peaks at 20 ExaFLOPS of FP8, and for inference, 40 ExaFLOPS of FP4. With 288 GB of HBM3E per GPU, the entire system has access to 1.1 PB.
5ddb2588e2: GPD has published the specifications for its WIN Mini Ultra gaming handheld, powered by Intel’s Arc G3 Extreme processor. We previously covered this model in October when GPD confirmed the processor and early specifications appeared online.

The WIN Mini Ultra uses Intel’s Panther Lake-based Arc G3 Extreme processor with 14 CPU cores (2P+8E+4LPE) and a maximum boost clock of 4.7 GHz. Its integrated Arc B390 graphics feature 12 Xe3 cores running at up to 2.3 GHz. GPD lists a configurable power range of 15W to 45W, supported by a cooling system with two fans and four heat pipes.

The handheld features an 8-inch LTPS IPS display with a 1920×1200 resolution, 120Hz refresh rate and variable refresh rate support from 48Hz to 120Hz. The panel also supports 10-point touch input, an anti-glare surface treatment and up to 575 nits brightness. GPD offers 32GB and 64GB LPDDR5X-8533 memory configurations, alongside an M.2 2280 PCIe 5.0 x4 SSD slot and microSD Express expansion.

GPD has equipped the WIN Mini Ultra with two USB4 v2.0 ports, each supporting up to 80Gbps bandwidth, DisplayPort 2.1 and USB Power Delivery. Additional connectivity includes a USB-A 10Gbps port, a 3.5mm audio jack and Intel AX211 Wi-Fi 6E. The device also includes capacitive joysticks with an 8KHz sampling rate, Hall effect triggers, a precision touchpad and a built-in keyboard.
d1f90614e7: Memory prices have already increased substantially over the past year, but TeamGroup believes the worst is yet to come. According to the company’s CEO, Gerry Chen, the shortage could become so severe in 2027 that even customers willing to pay higher prices may not be able to secure memory.

During TeamGroup’s November 2 earnings conference, Chen warned that the most difficult period would extend from the fourth quarter of 2026 through the second quarter of 2027. According to Taiwan’s Economic Daily News, the executive expects available memory inventory to become increasingly limited over the next three quarters. The company does not expect supply and demand to return to balance until the second half of 2028 at the earliest.

The situation is largely attributed to demand from AI servers and data centers. Major memory manufacturers, including Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, are allocating more production resources to high-bandwidth memory (HBM), DDR5 and server products. This has reduced capacity available for DDR4 and other consumer applications.

“By then [Q4 2026 – end of Q2 2027], even having money may not be enough to buy memory.” […] “Right now, you can still buy memory, but it’s expensive. After a while, you might not be able to buy it at all.”
45c5650230: Rubin HPC puts "over 50,000" CUDA cores on a chip, implies four-die layout

To accelerate those most demanding workloads, Nvidia says Rubin HPC has the highest number of CUDA cores on any of its GPUs - "more than 50,000" - which might imply that this chip uses a configuration similar to the four-die Rubin Ultra GPU, which links those dies together using NVLink-C2C.

Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package. Nvidia didn't reveal more details of the chip's physical layout alongside the announcement. (The representative image shared by the company wouldn't appear to take this into account.)

To keep data moving between Rubin HPC GPUs, Nvidia will use its NVLink 7 interconnect. The company didn't share any new details of the bandwidth or physical layer of this interconnect within the rack, but past disclosures about the tech have indicated that it retains the 3.6 TB/s of per-GPU bandwidth that NVLink 6 delivers while enlarging the size of its scale-up domain.
